note.title: DNB
note.p: Likely to be the second eldest son of Thomas Morton and brother of Edw. Morton, the former being in the DNB.

Entries to E/ED/Edw Morton, M Morton have been coded but with less certainty than is the case for Thomas Morton: E and M Morton do seem to be related, appearing together on three occasions. It seems likely that they are the two eldest sons of Thomas Morton. This assumes that the second son, John Maddison Morton, born 3 January 1811, died 19 December 1891,was known to Godwin by his middle name (but several of his obituaries do refer to him as Maddison Morton). It seems that Godwin first meets Maddison Morton on his own, aged 16, at the Kenney's. Some months later he meets '4 Mortons' at the Kenneys. Moreover, the vast majority of entries for 3 or 4 Mortons and for E and M Morton are in relation to the Kenneys, with whom the family seems to be close The use of E and M Morton may be driven by alphabetical order, but may also indicate that E is the older of the two.
16.11.1827 M Morton
18.3.1828 Edw. Morton
25.3.1829 E and M Morton
29.12.1829 Ed. Morton
18.10.1830 M Morton
26.5.1831 M Morton
13.9.1831 E and M Morton
18.6.1832 E and M Morton
Cases of '3 Mortons' and '4 Mortons' have also been taken to include both E and M Morton. Cases of 'Mortons' may well include the two sons, but they might simply refer to Morton and his wife. On these grounds, they have not been coded as including them.
